facts.raw_span: A patient in their late 40s was admitted to the hospital to receive a uterine myomectomy procedure
no history of structural heart disease, hypertension, myocarditis, or sleep apnea syndrome
denied a family history of cardiovascular disease and sudden death
no significant abnormalities
Normal levels of whole blood cells count, electrolytes, myocardial enzymes, and brain natriuretic peptide
Initial 12-lead ECG showed no abnormalities
Chest radiographic imaging showed no abnormalities
Echocardiographic findings showed no abnormalities
Holter monitor recording: Recording showed a 23.8-second ventricular asystole during syncope
gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction followed by complete atrioventricular block
Asystole derived from gradually extended PR and PP intervals and was transiently suspended by a spontaneous junctional escape beat
Electrophysiologic studies: Showed no abnormalities in the cardiac conduction system
